editor.title: CV scoring rubric
editor.hint: CVs are scored strictly against these criteria: the AI reads the CV, picks a band from your anchors and answers each checklist item with a quote — it never gives a number. The final score comes from this job's formula in the "Scoring formula" block below. Without a rubric no CV can be scored.
editor.aiNeedsContent: Enter the position and a description or candidate requirements before asking AI.
editor.replaceConfirm: Replace the current criteria with the new ones?
editor.noTemplates: No templates yet — HR Admins add them on the Playbook screen.
editor.name: Criterion name
editor.guidePlaceholder: What does a strong candidate show in the CV?
editor.levelsHint: Describe each score band concretely (years, technologies, measurable results) so AI scores consistently.

levelPlaceholder.excellent: e.g. 4+ years shipping real products, technical leadership
levelPlaceholder.good: e.g. 2–4 years in the same domain
levelPlaceholder.fair: e.g. Under 2 years or an adjacent domain

problems.badWeight: Each scored criterion needs a weight greater than 0.
problems.total: Weights of the scored criteria must add up to 100 (currently {{total}}).
problems.missingGuide: Each scored criterion needs a scoring guide or at least one score band.
problems.tooManyChecks: At most 8 checklist items per criterion.
problems.noScored: At least one scored criterion is required — required conditions do not produce a score.
problems.badMinScore: A criterion minimum must be a whole number from 1 to 100.
problems.badCheckWeight: Checklist item weights can only be ×1, ×2 or ×3.

editor.empty: No criteria yet. Use "AI suggest", pick a company template, import Excel or add them manually.
editor.error: Something went wrong. Please try again.

checks.title: Checklist ({{count}})
checks.hint: The AI only answers yes/no per item with a quote; the score inside the band = band floor + (weight of items met ÷ weight of items answered) × band width.
checks.emptyHint: No checklist yet — the AI will estimate where the score sits inside the band. Add 3–5 signals verifiable from a CV so two CVs in the same band are ranked correctly.
checks.readOnlyTitle: Checklist (decides the score inside the band):

kind.knockoutHint: The AI only answers Met / Not met with a quote from the CV; if the CV does not mention it, it is not met. Not met → recommendation "Not a fit", but the score is still calculated and the application is never rejected automatically. Use only for truly essential requirements (licences, mandatory certificates…).
kind.notePlaceholder: Note for the AI (optional) — e.g. equivalent international certificates are accepted

editor.minScoreHint: Optional — if this criterion scores below it, the recommendation becomes "Not a fit" even with a high total (the score is kept, the application is not rejected automatically).

position.title: Score inside the band

status.pass: All required conditions and minimums are met.
status.fail: At least one condition failed — the recommendation is forced to "Not a fit". The score is kept; the application is not rejected automatically.
status.review: Some conditions could not be verified from the CV — a person should check them. The recommendation is not forced.

reason.knockout_failed: The CV does not show this condition is met.
reason.knockout_unverified: The AI could not verify it (no supporting quote) — check manually.
reason.below_min_score: Below the minimum the Hiring Manager set for this criterion.
reason.min_score_unscored: The criterion produced no score — check manually.

interviewEditor.hint: The AI scores the candidate's answers against exactly these criteria: 0–100 per criterion, then a weighted average compared with the job's pass mark. Without criteria the interview produces no report.
interviewEditor.guidePlaceholder: What does a strong answer show?
interviewEditor.levelsHint: Describe answers in each score band (correct fundamentals, real examples, trade-offs…) so the AI scores consistently.

levelPlaceholder.excellent: E.g. Explains the fundamentals correctly, covers trade-offs and edge cases
levelPlaceholder.good: E.g. Gets the main points right with an example, but not in depth
levelPlaceholder.fair: E.g. Partly right, some concepts confused
levelPlaceholder.poor: E.g. Wrong or unable to answer

formula.title: Scoring formula
formula.hint: The Hiring Manager decides how the AI's answers become a score and a recommendation. Changing the formula (not the criterion text) recalculates scores immediately from the existing AI results — no AI re-scoring.
formula.inBand: Each criterion = band floor + (weight of items met ÷ weight of items answered) × band width; criteria the AI could not score are left out of both numerator and denominator.
formula.modelCompensatory: Compensatory model: a high score on one criterion can make up for a low score on another. Add required conditions or per-criterion minimums to stop that.
formula.modelHybrid: Hybrid model (compensatory + conditions). The recommendation is forced to "Not a fit" if:
formula.gatesNote: The score is still calculated and shown; the application is never rejected automatically.
formula.bandsHint: The AI picks a band from your anchors; the thresholds decide how many points that band is worth. Each band must be at least 5 points wide.
formula.tiersHint: Compared with the (rounded) total CV score.

problems.badBands: Band thresholds must be whole numbers in decreasing order: Excellent > Good > Partial > 0, with Excellent below 100.
problems.bandTooNarrow: Each band must be at least 5 points wide.
problems.badTiers: Recommendation thresholds must be whole numbers in decreasing order within 1–100: Strong fit > Good fit > Consider.

formula.summaryBands: Bands: Excellent {{excellent}} · Good {{good}} · Partial {{fair}} · Not met {{poor}}
formula.summaryTiers: Recommendation: Strong fit from {{strong}} · Good fit from {{hire}} · Consider from {{caution}}
formula.sourcesHint: The parameters follow the common frame of recruitment guidance: screen out on required conditions → score on an anchored scale → weighted sum → compare with thresholds.

sources.opm: US OPM — Training & Experience Evaluations: screen minimum requirements before scoring
sources.uwyo: University of Wyoming — Hiring Matrix: evidence-anchored scale, ×1/×2/×3 weights, minimums as a gate
sources.fourCorner: 4 Corner Resources — Resume Screening Scorecard: weights and advancement thresholds per role
sources.zythr: ZYTHR — Weighted Candidate Scoring Matrix: mandatory vs graded criteria, calibrate on past applicants
sources.libretexts: LibreTexts HRM — Testing and Selecting: compensatory, multiple cutoff, multiple hurdle models
sources.ticnote: TicNote — How to Score Resumes Objectively: knockout lane vs scored lane, tiered thresholds
